- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days) are common; cap forecast at 10-15% above peak for next 5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– > 0.10); add 2-3% buffer to forecast mean.
- If last 3 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture continuation; extend upward bias by 1-2% for next 5 days.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00–0.05) and price is trending, model often lags; forecast 1-2 days ahead of actual trend.
- When sentiment is consistently low and price is rising, model underreacts; increase forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day.
